title: Spiritual Discipline and the Order of Virtues
english: Today is a feast and I drink wine, and tomorrow is Pentecost and I will eat meat, because there is no feast among monks, nor is there to fill a man's belly.

Passover is the Lord's passing over from evil, but Pentecost is the resurrection of the soul. The feast of God is the forgiveness of evils, but he who holds a grudge will receive grief. The Lord's Pentecost is the resurrection of love, but he who hates his brother will fall as a shameful corpse. The feast of God is true knowledge, but he who attends to false knowledge will end shamefully.
Fasting with a pure heart is better than a feast in the impurity of the soul. He who casts out evil thoughts from his heart is like one who fixes his infants to the rock.

A monk who is sleepy will fall into evils, but he who is watchful will be like a sparrow. Do not give yourself in watchfulness to empty narratives, and do not cast away spiritual words, for the Lord observes your soul and will by no means acquit you from every evil.
Much sleep thickens the mind, but watchfulness thins it. Much sleep brings temptations, but he who is watchful will flee them. Just as fire melts wax, so good watchfulness [melts] evil thoughts.

A man sleeping is better than a monk watching over vain thoughts. An angelic dream rejoices the heart, but a demonic dream disturbs it. Repentance and humility straightened the soul, but almsgiving and meekness established it.

Remember through all things your exodus and do not forget the eternal judgment, and there will not be deficiency in your soul. If a spirit of acedia rises upon you, do not leave your house, and do not turn away in time, for again you will benefit. For in whatever way if someone [is] white silver, so shall your heart be made bright. The spirit of acedia drives away tears, but the spirit of sorrow crushes prayer. Desiring wealth, he will care...
To many things, and enduring them, one suffers bitter griefs.

Let no scorpion linger in your lap, and no evil thought in your heart. Do not spare the killing of the offspring of serpents (Matt 3:7), and do not give birth to the thoughts of their hearts. Just as fire tests silver and gold, so trials test the heart of a monk. Remove from yourself pride, and make vanity a great distance from you. For he who fails in glory will be grieved, but he who succeeds will be proud. Do not give your heart to pride, and do not say before the face of God, 'I am capable,' lest the Lord abandon your soul, and evil demons humble it. For then your enemies will cause you to fly through the air, and terrible nights will receive you.

Knowledge guards the citizenship of the monk, but he who descends from knowledge will fall among robbers. From a spiritual rock a river flows, and a practical soul drinks from it. A pure soul is a vessel of election, but the unclean one will be filled with bitterness. Without milk a child will not be nourished, and without apatheia a heart will not be exalted. Before love comes apatheia, and before knowledge comes love. To knowledge wisdom is added, and from prudence apatheia is brought forth. The fear of the Lord generates prudence (Ps 118:7), and faith in Christ grants the fear of God. A burning arrow sets the soul on fire, but a practical man will extinguish it. Knowledge turns away from a cry and blasphemy, and wisdom flees from deceitful words. Honey is soft and wax is sweet, but the knowledge of God is sweeter than both.

Listen, monk, to the words of your father, and do not make his instructions void. Wherever he may send you, follow him and accompany him according to your understanding. For by this method you will escape evil thoughts, and evil demons will not be strong against you. If silver trusts you, you will not scatter it, and even if it works, you will give it back.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Sentences on Obedience and Discipline
english: A wicked steward will crush the souls of brothers, and a slanderer will not show them mercy. He who scatters the monastery's existing possessions wrongs God, and he who neglects them will not go unpunished. 76 An unjust steward divides [the resources] poorly, but the just one will give according to worth. 77 He who slanders his brother will be destroyed, and he who neglects the weak will not see light. 78 A worldly man, better at serving his own weakness, is worse than a recluse who does not pity his neighbor. 79 A foolish monk will neglect the tools of his craft, but the wise one will take care of them.

80 Do not say: 'I will stay today and leave tomorrow,' for you have not reasoned wisely about this. 81 A wandering monk will meditate on false sayings, and he will contradict his own father. 82 He who beautifies his clothes and fills his belly pastures shameful thoughts and does not sit with the temperate. 83 If you enter a village, do not approach women and do not engage in talk with them. For as one casts a hook, so your soul will be drawn. 84 A long-suffering monk will be loved, but he who provokes his brothers will be hated. 85 A gentle monk is loved by the Lord, but he will cast away the bold. 86 A lazy monk will grumble much, and a sleepy one will pretend to have a headache.

87 If your brother is grieved, comfort him, and if he suffers, suffer with him. For by doing this you gladden his heart, and you will store up a great treasure in heaven. 88 A monk who leaves his father's words unguarded will blaspheme him for having fathered many, and will slander the lives of his children, but the Lord will make him nothing. 89 He who seeks praise is separated from brothers, and he blames his own father. 90 Do not give ear to...
Speak according to your father and do not stir up the soul by dishonoring him, so that the Lord may not be angry at your works and erase your name from the book of the living (Ps 69:6).
91 He who obeys his father loves himself, but he who argues against him will fall into evils.
92 Blessed is the monk who guards the commandments of the Lord, and holy is the one who maintains the words of his fathers.
93 A lazy monk will suffer much loss, but if he is courageous and adds to his form.
94 He who guards his tongue straightens his paths (Prov 4:25), and he who keeps his heart will be filled with knowledge.
95 A double-tongued monk disturbs brothers, but the faithful one brings stillness.
96 He who trusts in his own self-control will fall, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.
97 Do not give yourself to the gluttony of the belly, and do not be filled with nocturnal sleep. For by this way you will become pure and the spirit of the Lord will come upon you.
98 While singing, the mind becomes still, and while being long-suffering, it will be unshakeable.
99 From gentleness knowledge is born, and from audacity ignorance.
100 Just as water increases a plant, so the humbling of the mind exalts the heart.
101 While searching for banquets, the lamp will be extinguished, and his soul will see darkness.
102 Bind your bread with a yoke and drink your water in measure, and the spirit of fornication will flee from you.
103 Give wine to those becoming old and offer food to those growing weak, because they have worn out the flesh of their youth.
104 Do not look down upon your brother and do not rejoice in his fall. For the Lord knows your heart and will deliver you in the day of death.
105 A wise monk will be impassive, but the fool will exhaust himself with evils.
106 The Lord blinds an evil eye, but he rescues the simple from darkness.
107 Just as the Morning Star is in heaven and just as the phoenix is in paradise, so in a gentle soul is a pure mind.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Warning against false doctrines
english: A wise man searches for the words of God, but the foolish one will be mocked by them. He who hates the knowledge of God and pushes away His contemplation is like a spear piercing his own heart. Knowledge of the Trinity is superior to the knowledge of the incorporeal ones, and the contemplation of it is superior to the words of all the ages.

Many are the elders of practice, but their life is the knowledge of truth. A young man of practice bears much, but who will respect an undaunted elder? I saw an angry elder exalting himself upon his throne, but rather his young man had hope.

He who scandalizes the worldly ones will not be without punishment, and he who provokes them insults his own name. He who disturbs the church of the Lord will be consumed by fire, and he who opposes a priest will be swallowed by the earth. He who loves the bee will eat its wax, and he who gathers it will be filled with spirit.

Honor the Lord and you will know the words of the incorporeal, and serve Him and He will show you the words of the ages. Apart from knowledge, the heart will not be exalted, and a tree will not bloom without drink.

The flesh of Christ is the practical virtues, and he who eats them will become impassive. The blood of Christ is the contemplation of things that have come to pass, and he who drinks it will be made wise by it. The breast of the Lord is the knowledge of God, and he who falls upon it will be a theologian. The Gnostic and the practical met one another, but the Lord stands in the middle of both.

He who has acquired love has acquired a treasure, and has received grace from the Lord. Wisdom recognizes the dogmas of demons, but prudence tracks out their cunning. Do not reject the holy dogmas which your fathers laid down, and do not abandon the faith of your baptism, and do not cast away the spiritual seal, so that the Lord may be born in your soul and cover you in the day of evil. The words of heretics are angels of death, and he who receives them [text ends abruptly]...

[He] will lose his own soul. Now then, son, listen to me, and do not approach the doors of lawless men, nor walk upon their snares, so that you may not be caught. But turn your soul away from false knowledge. For I have often spoken to them, but I traced out their dark words, and I found a venom of shields among them. There is no prudence and there is no wisdom in their words. All those receiving them will be destroyed, and those loving them will be filled with evils. I saw the father of their dogmas and encountered them in the desert. For enemies of the Lord met me, and demons contended with me in words, and I did not see true light in their utterances.

127 A man lying will fall from God, and deceiving his neighbor will fall into evils. 128 Better is the paradise of God than a garden of vegetables, and the river of the Lord than a great river flooding the earth. 5 129 More trustworthy is heavenly water than the water of Egyptians wise men drawing from the earth. 130 Just as those ascending the wheels go down, so those exalting their words are humbled in them. 131 The wisdom of the Lord lifts up the heart, but his prudence cleanses it.

132 Words of providence are dark, and contemplations of judgment are hard to understand, but a practical man will know them. 133 Purifying himself, he will see noetic natures, and the words of the incorporeal he will know, alone, gentle. 134 The creature saying the Holy Trinity blasphemes God, and he who rejects his Christ will not know him. 135 Contemplations of worlds widen the heart, but words of providence and judgment lift it up. 136 Knowledge of the incorporeal lifts up the mind and presents it to the Holy Trinity. 137 Remember the clear proverbs of what has been given to you in the Lord, and do not forget my humble soul in the time of prayer. 6
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
